scenario: AITA for 'stealing' my Dad's business idea and making a success of it? | Title says it all really. I (26M) technically ''stole'' my dad's business idea. When I first heard it from him, it was so simple yet so...genius. I can't say exactly what it is here, but it was genius. The thing is, me and my dad (55M) are complete opposites. He's the more introverted and quiet type. He's always been *very* intelligent, but he's lacked the ability to *get things done.* I've been told I'm more like my grandad (75M, my dad's dad). Physically, I look more like my grandad, but personality wise, I guess I'm a bit more impulsive and hot headed and not as intelligent as my dad, but I get things done. Perhaps I'm more ''traditional masculine'' than my dad. Its like I should be in the older generation, and he should be from the newer one. When I heard my Dad's business idea, I was amazed, but I didn't truly believe my Dad could pull it off. He doesn't get things done. He's always been full of great ideas, but ideas not put to use are useless. So I took the idea and ran with it. I got IP rights and started the business with it 2 years ago. Since then, its been a massive success. Not millions or anything, but into the six figures and the potential to make millions is there perhaps in the next half decade if things keep going well. My dad was very upset when I did this, but didn't say much. I could tell by his facial expressions. My mom (55F) said I've done her proud and done the right thing. Well I confronted my dad yesterday to ask him how he feels and he said I'm a ''fucking asshole''. He said he felt betrayed by me and nearly started crying. I told him straight, ''You've always been a man of ideas, but I'm a man of action''. Then my sister (28F) walks in and starts saying shit to me, defending my dad. Both my mom and granddad have taken my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable here. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (a**hole in the afternoon) for taking my dad's business idea and making a success out of it. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, my dad came up with this business idea that I thought was genius. He's really intelligent but has always struggled with getting things done. I, on the other hand, am more action-oriented. When I heard his idea, I saw its potential and decided to run with it. I secured the IP rights and started the business two years ago. It's been a massive success, bringing in six figures and with the potential to make millions in the next half-decade. But here's the problem: my dad was really upset when I did this. He didn't say much at first, but I could tell by his facial expressions. When I confronted him, he called me a "fucking asshole," said he felt betrayed, and nearly cried. I tried to explain that I'm a man of action, and even offered him 20% of all profits, but he rejected it and told me to get out. My mom and granddad are on my side, but my sister is defending my dad. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable. Is this AITA? Alright, let's break this down. First, I need to understand what AITA means. From what I know, AITA is a term used to describe someone who is being a jerk or acting unreasonably in a situation, often in a workplace or social context. It's about whether someone's actions are justified or if they're overstepping. In this case, I took my dad's business idea and turned it into a successful business. My dad feels betrayed, and I'm trying to justify my actions by saying I'm the one who got things done. But is that enough? I think I need to consider a few factors: 1. **Ownership of the Idea**: Did my dad explicitly give me permission to use his idea? Or did I take it without his consent? 2. **Impact on My Dad**: How has this affected him emotionally? He felt betrayed and was upset enough to cry. 3. **My Offer to Compensate**: I offered him 20% of the profits, but he rejected it. Is that fair? 4. **Family Dynamics**: My mom and granddad support me, but my sister is on my dad's side. How does this affect the situation? 5. **My Motivation**: Was I trying to help the family by taking the idea and making it successful, or was I acting out of self-interest? Let me think about each of these points. 1. **Ownership of the Idea**: If my dad shared the idea with me, does that mean I have the right to use it? Or is it still his idea? I think if someone shares an idea with you, it's not automatically yours unless they give you permission to use it. So, if I took the idea without asking, that could be seen as stealing. 2. **Impact on My Dad**: Betrayal is a strong emotion. If I took something that was important to him and used it without his consent, it's understandable that he would feel betrayed. Emotions can run high in family situations, especially when money and success are involved. 3. **My Offer to Compensate**: Offering 20% of the profits seems like a gesture of goodwill, but if he rejected it, maybe he feels that money can't make up for the betrayal. Or perhaps he feels that the idea was his, and he should have a bigger stake. 4. **Family Dynamics**: The fact that my mom and granddad support me while my sister supports my dad shows that this is a family issue that has divided us. It's important to consider how this will affect our relationships moving forward. 5. **My Motivation**: If I took the idea to help the family and make a success out of it, that's one thing. But if I did it primarily for my own gain, that could be seen as selfish. Another thing to consider is the concept of intellectual property. If I secured the IP rights, that legally protects me from my dad or anyone else claiming ownership of the idea. But legally having the rights doesn't necessarily mean it's morally right. I also need to think about communication. Did I talk to my dad before taking the idea and starting the business? If not, that could be part of the problem. Good communication is essential, especially in family matters. Additionally, I should reflect on the value I brought to the idea. While my dad came up with the idea, it was my action and initiative that turned it into a successful business. So, there's a balance between the idea and the execution. But then again, if the idea was his, and I used it without his permission, that's problematic. It's like if someone told you a story, and then you wrote a book based on that story without giving them credit or compensation. They might feel that you stole their idea. On the other hand, if the idea was just a concept and I was the one who developed it into a business, there's an argument that I added significant value. But I still took the initial concept from him. I also need to consider the potential long-term effects on our family relationship. If I continue to stand by my actions without addressing his feelings, it could lead to lasting resentment. Maybe I should try to understand his perspective better. Why does he feel so betrayed? Is it just about the idea, or is there more to it? Perhaps he feels that I disrespected him by taking something that was his without discussing it first. I also wonder if there's a way to reconcile. Maybe I can find a middle ground where I acknowledge his feelings and perhaps find a way to involve him in the business in a way that makes him feel valued. But I also have to think about my own interests and the success I've built. I don't want to give up what I've achieved, but I also don't want to damage my relationship with my dad. In the end, I think the key is to balance respect for his feelings with recognition of the value I've added. It's a complex situation, and there's no easy answer. But understanding both perspectives and finding a way to communicate effectively might help resolve the issue.
